name: California
summary: California is nominally at-will, but it is the most heavily regulated US state for employers. It has daily overtime, meal and rest premiums, strict final-pay timing, PAGA representative penalties, a broad FEHA (5+ employees), pay-scale disclosure, annual pay data reporting, and CCPA privacy rights that fully cover employee and applicant data. It also changes faster than any other state: 2026 brought SB 642 (pay scale = good-faith estimate; stock and benefits count as 'wages' under the Equal Pay Act), AB 692 (ban on stay-or-pay repayment clauses), SB 294 (annual Know Your Rights notice), SB 513 (training records in personnel files), and CPPA risk-assessment rules, with ADMT obligations starting 1 Jan 2027. US-HQ tech and semiconductor employers most often go wrong by using national templates with non-competes, non-CA choice-of-law clauses or training-repayment clauses, by misclassifying engineers and technicians as exempt, by missing final-pay deadlines at layoffs, and by treating HR data as outside CCPA.

ratingNotes.termination: At-will with no statutory severance, but immediate final pay, waiting-time penalties, Cal-WARN (75+ employees, 50+ layoffs), a 90-day retaliation presumption and plaintiff-friendly FEHA/public-policy claims raise the risk.
ratingNotes.representation: No works councils, and union density in tech is low; SB 399 (captive-audience ban) and AB 288 (PERB backstop) are both enjoined, but the labor-law landscape is unsettled.
ratingNotes.privacy: Only US state where the full CCPA applies to employee and applicant data; CPPA risk-assessment/ADMT rules, CRD ADS rules, a constitutional privacy right and all-party-consent recording add to it.
ratingNotes.payTransparency: Pay scale in every posting (15+ employees), salary history ban, annual CRD pay data reports (100+) with mandatory penalties, and an Equal Pay Act covering sex, race and ethnicity with a 6-year lookback.
ratingNotes.workingTime: Daily OT (over 8) and double time (over 12), 7th-day rules, meal/rest premiums, exempt salary floor of 2x minimum wage, and PAGA exposure for technical violations.
ratingNotes.leave: Many overlapping job-protected leaves (CFRA, PDL, PSL, bereavement, reproductive loss, victims, school, donor, military spouse), plus SDI/PFL wage replacement and local sick-leave ordinances.
ratingNotes.immigration: Visas are federal, but state rules add employer duties: SB 294 notices, I-9 inspection notice (LC 90.2), E-Verify limits (LC 1019.2) and no voluntary ICE access to non-public areas.
ratingNotes.changeVelocity: Dozens of employment bills are enacted every year, many effective 1 January, plus CRD, CPPA and Cal/OSHA rulemaking; several 2026 bills await the Governor (deadline 30 Sept 2026).

keyFacts.label: Employment model
keyFacts.value: At-will (Labor Code 2922), subject to FEHA (5+ employees), claims for wrongful termination in violation of public policy, implied-contract claims, and IWC Wage Order 4 for professional, technical and clerical work. PAGA lets employees sue for civil penalties on behalf of the state.

keyFacts.label: Contracts & offer letters
keyFacts.value: No written contract is required, but non-exempt hires need a Labor Code 2810.5 wage notice, and commission plans must be in writing (LC 2751). Offer letters must not include non-competes (B&P 16600), non-California law or forum clauses (LC 925), or stay-or-pay repayment terms (AB 692). Invention-assignment agreements need the LC 2870 carve-out notice.

keyFacts.label: Probation
keyFacts.value: No statutory probation. Any 'introductory period' should say it does not change at-will status. The PSL 90-day use wait and CFRA eligibility (12 months and 1,250 hours) run on their own schedules.

keyFacts.label: Notice (employer)
keyFacts.value: No notice is required for individual terminations. Cal-WARN requires 60 days' notice for a mass layoff (50+ in 30 days), relocation or termination at a covered establishment (75+ employees). Written notice of the change in employment status (UI Code 1089) is due immediately at separation.

keyFacts.label: Notice (employee)
keyFacts.value: No notice is required. Giving at least 72 hours' notice of resignation means final pay is due on the last day; without notice, final pay is due within 72 hours (LC 202).

keyFacts.label: Statutory severance
keyFacts.value: None. Cal-WARN violations cost up to 60 days' back pay and benefits (or half the employee's tenure if shorter) plus civil penalties of up to $500/day; there is no separate Cal-WARN pay entitlement when notice is given. Severance is market practice, usually exchanged for a release.

keyFacts.label: Working hours & overtime
keyFacts.value: 1.5x after 8 hours/day or 40/week and for the first 8 hours on the 7th consecutive day; 2x after 12 hours/day or 8 hours on the 7th day. Meal break of 30 minutes before the end of the 5th hour; 10-minute rest per 4 hours or major fraction; one hour of premium pay per missed break. Exempt salary floor is $70,304 (2026) and $72,384 (2027); the computer-professional exemption requires $58.85/hr or $122,573.13/yr (2026).

keyFacts.label: Minimum wage
keyFacts.value: $16.90/hr statewide from 1 Jan 2026 and $17.40 from 1 Jan 2027 (DIR). Bay Area local rates are higher: Sunnyvale $19.50, Mountain View $19.70, Santa Clara/Palo Alto/Cupertino $18.70, San Jose $18.45 (2026). SF, LA and Berkeley adjust on 1 July.

keyFacts.label: Annual leave
keyFacts.value: Vacation is not mandatory. Once offered, it vests as earned, cannot be forfeited ('use-it-or-lose-it' is unlawful) and must be paid out at termination (LC 227.3; Suastez). Accrual caps are allowed. 'Unlimited' PTO must be truly unlimited to avoid payout exposure.

keyFacts.label: Public holidays
keyFacts.value: No private-sector requirement to give paid holidays or pay holiday premiums. Employers must allow up to 2 hours' paid time off to vote when needed (Elections Code 14000) and post the voting-time notice 10 days before statewide elections.

keyFacts.label: Sick leave
keyFacts.value: Paid sick leave (LC 245-249): employees may use at least 40 hours/5 days a year (SB 616, since 2024). Accrual is 1 hour per 30 worked, with a cap of at least 80 hours/10 days, or the employer can front-load; there is no payout at termination. Leave can be used for AB 406 reasons such as jury, witness and victim court proceedings. Local ordinances (SF, LA, Oakland, Berkeley, San Diego, etc.) can be more generous.

keyFacts.label: Parental leave
keyFacts.value: PDL gives up to 4 months per pregnancy (5+ employees). CFRA gives 12 weeks for bonding or family care (5+ employees; 12 months and 1,250 hours); PDL and CFRA do not run concurrently. PFL replaces 70-90% of wages (since 2025) for up to 8 weeks but is not job-protected. Reproductive-loss leave is 5 days; lactation accommodation also applies.

keyFacts.label: Social insurance / mandatory benefits
keyFacts.value: SDI (covers DI and PFL) is employee-paid at 1.3% of all wages in 2026, with no wage cap since 2024. UI and ETT (0.1%) are employer-paid on the first $7,000 per employee. Workers' comp is mandatory. CalSavers applies unless a qualified plan such as a 401(k) is offered and an exemption is filed. Federal FICA/FUTA also apply; check the current FUTA credit reduction.

keyFacts.label: Payroll frequency & final pay
keyFacts.value: Non-exempt staff must be paid at least semi-monthly on designated paydays (LC 204); exempt staff may be paid monthly. On discharge or layoff, all wages including accrued vacation are due immediately. On resignation, pay is due within 72 hours without notice or on the last day with 72+ hours' notice. Waiting-time penalties are up to 30 days' wages (LC 203).

keyFacts.label: Employee representation
keyFacts.value: The NLRA governs private-sector labor relations. There are no works councils or consultation duties. SB 399's captive-audience ban (LC 1137) and AB 288's PERB backstop are both preliminarily enjoined (2025) and still being litigated. Union density among semiconductor and tech employees is low.

keyFacts.label: Data privacy law
keyFacts.value: Since 1 Jan 2023, CCPA/CPRA covers employee, applicant and contractor data, with notice at collection, rights requests, sensitive-data limits and a retention schedule. CPPA rules (effective 1 Jan 2026) add risk assessments now, ADMT duties from 1 Jan 2027 and cybersecurity audits from 1 Apr 2028. Also relevant: the constitutional privacy right (Art. I §1), CMIA medical confidentiality, and all-party consent for recording (Penal Code 632).

keyFacts.label: Record retention
keyFacts.value: Payroll and wage statements: 3 years (LC 226, 1174). Personnel files: 3 years after termination (LC 1198.5). Applications, personnel records and ADS data: 4 years (Gov Code 12946; CRD regs). Job title/wage history: employment plus 3 years (LC 432.3). WVPP incident and hazard records: 5 years (training 1 year). Harassment training: 2 years. SB 294 notices: 3 years.

keyFacts.label: Non-competes & IP
keyFacts.value: Non-competes and most non-solicits are void (B&P 16600), even when signed out of state (16600.5); employers had to notify affected employees by 14 Feb 2024 (16600.1). LC 925 bars non-CA law or forum. Invention assignment is limited by LC 2870-2872. Stay-or-pay clauses are barred by AB 692 (B&P 16608 / LC 926). Trade secrets are protected under CUTSA (Civ. Code 3426).

keyFacts.label: Language requirements
keyFacts.value: No general English-only or translation rule for contracts. However, the LC 2810.5 notice must be in the language the employer normally uses to communicate, EEO/harassment policies must be translated into any language spoken by 10%+ of a facility's workforce (2 CCR 11023), and the SB 294 notice must be given in the employee's usual work language when a state template exists.

keyFacts.label: Regulator(s)
keyFacts.value: Labor Commissioner/DLSE and DIR (wage-hour, PSL, SB 294); Civil Rights Department (FEHA, CFRA/PDL, pay data, harassment training); EDD (payroll taxes, SDI/PFL, Cal-WARN); Cal/OSHA and the OSH Standards Board; CPPA and the Attorney General (CCPA); LWDA (PAGA notices); CalSavers.

mandatoryPolicies.name: EEO / anti-harassment / anti-retaliation policy
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Written policy (5+ employees) that lists all FEHA-protected categories, gives a complaint process with alternatives to the direct supervisor, and commits to confidentiality, timely and impartial investigation, remedial action and non-retaliation. Distribute with acknowledgment and translate into any language spoken by 10%+ of a facility's workforce.

mandatoryPolicies.name: Harassment prevention training
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: 5+ employees: 2 hours for supervisors and 1 hour for non-supervisors, within 6 months of hire or promotion and every 2 years after; seasonal/temporary staff within 30 days or 100 hours. Must cover abusive conduct, gender identity/expression and sexual orientation. Keep records 2 years.

mandatoryPolicies.name: Injury & Illness Prevention Program (IIPP)
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: All employers must have a written IIPP: a responsible person, hazard assessment and correction, training, communication, compliance enforcement and recordkeeping.

mandatoryPolicies.name: Workplace Violence Prevention Plan (WVPP)
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Written, site-specific plan developed with employee involvement, plus annual interactive training, a violent incident log, post-incident investigation, and hazard records kept 5 years (training 1 year). Exemptions include sites closed to the public with fewer than 10 employees and remote workers.

mandatoryPolicies.name: Heat illness prevention (indoor/outdoor)
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Written plan where indoor work areas reach 82°F. Assessment and controls are required at 87°F, or at 82°F where employees wear clothing that restricts heat removal or work near high radiant heat.

mandatoryPolicies.name: Lactation accommodation policy
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Policy stating the right to lactation accommodation, how to request it, the employer's duty to respond, and the right to complain to the Labor Commissioner. Include it in the handbook and give it to new hires and to anyone asking about parental leave.

mandatoryPolicies.name: Paid sick leave policy
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Accrual or front-load method giving at least 40 hours/5 days of use a year, the balance shown on each wage statement, and all statutory reasons for use (including AB 406 jury, witness and victim reasons). Check local ordinances.

mandatoryPolicies.name: CFRA / PDL leave policy
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Employers with 5+ employees that have a handbook must describe CFRA and PDL rights in it; otherwise give notice when leave is requested. Post the CRD notices.

mandatoryPolicies.name: Bereavement & reproductive loss leave
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Up to 5 days bereavement within 3 months of a family member's death, and up to 5 days per reproductive-loss event (max 20 days in 12 months), with confidentiality (5+ employees).

mandatoryPolicies.name: Survivors of violence / victims' leave notice
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Covers leave and safety accommodations for victims of qualifying acts of violence and jury/witness leave. The CRD notice goes to employees at hire, annually, on request, and when an employee discloses victim status (notice duty applies to 25+ employers — verify threshold).

mandatoryPolicies.name: Workplace Know Your Rights notice & emergency contact
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Stand-alone notice using the Labor Commissioner template, given to all employees by 1 Feb each year and at hire, and sent to any union. Let employees designate an emergency contact to be notified if they are arrested or detained at work. Keep records 3 years.

mandatoryPolicies.name: Employee/applicant privacy notice & policy
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Covered businesses must give a notice at collection (categories, purposes, retention period per category, sale/sharing) and a privacy policy, and must handle rights requests from employees, applicants and contractors.
mandatoryPolicies.source: Civ. Code 1798.100 et seq. (CCPA/CPRA); 11 CCR 7000 et seq.

mandatoryPolicies.name: Pay transparency / pay scale procedure
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: 15+ employees must post a good-faith pay range in every job posting, including third-party postings. All employers must give the pay scale for an employee's current role on request, never ask about salary history, and keep job title and wage history for employment plus 3 years.

mandatoryPolicies.name: Pay data reporting
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: 100+ employees must file the annual CRD pay data report by the second Wednesday of May, plus a separate report if they use 100+ workers through labor contractors. Store demographic data separately from personnel files (SB 464).

mandatoryPolicies.name: Fair chance (criminal history) hiring procedure
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: 5+ employees: no criminal history inquiries before a conditional offer. Afterwards, an individualized assessment, preliminary notice with 5 business days to respond, and a final written notice. Follow local ordinances such as SF and LA County.

mandatoryPolicies.name: Restrictive covenant & invention assignment compliance
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: No non-competes or non-CA law/forum clauses. Invention assignment agreements must include the written LC 2870 notice. Confidentiality and non-disparagement terms must carve out disclosure of unlawful workplace conduct.

mandatoryPolicies.name: Repayment / stay-or-pay agreements
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: For agreements from 1 Jan 2026, departing workers cannot be required to repay training, relocation or other costs, or pay quit fees. Narrow exceptions cover transferable-credential tuition and discretionary upfront bonuses under standalone agreements. $5,000 per worker minimum damages.

mandatoryPolicies.name: Meal & rest period policy
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Brinker-compliant policy for non-exempt staff: provide and authorize breaks, record meal periods, pay premiums automatically at the regular rate, and handle any on-duty meal agreements properly.

mandatoryPolicies.name: Expense reimbursement policy
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Reimburse all necessary business expenses, including a reasonable share of personal phone and internet for remote or hybrid work. The right cannot be waived.

mandatoryPolicies.name: Vacation / PTO policy
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Accrual caps are allowed, but forfeiture of accrued time is not. Pay out at termination. Define rules for any unlimited PTO carefully.

mandatoryPolicies.name: Whistleblower / non-retaliation policy
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Protect internal and external reports of legal violations. Post the Labor Commissioner's whistleblower notice with the hotline number. Retaliation is presumed if adverse action follows protected activity within 90 days.

mandatoryPolicies.name: Drug & cannabis testing policy
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: No discrimination for off-duty cannabis use or for non-psychoactive metabolite results, and no questions about past cannabis use. Exceptions cover security clearance or federal background-check roles and federally mandated testing.

mandatoryPolicies.name: Reasonable accommodation / interactive process
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Written procedure for disability, pregnancy and religious accommodation requests, including those arising from AI/ADS assessments.

mandatoryPolicies.name: Electronic monitoring & acceptable use policy
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Disclose monitoring in the CCPA notice. No audio or video recording in restrooms or locker rooms. All-party consent for recording confidential communications. No demands for access to personal social media.

mandatoryPolicies.name: Records retention schedule
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: The CCPA notice must state a retention period per category of personal information. Align it with the minimums in LC 226/1174/1198.5, Gov Code 12946 (4 years) and CRD ADS rules (4 years).

hiring.detail: Every posting for a role that may be filled in California, including remote roles and third-party postings, must show a good-faith estimate of the base salary or hourly range the employer reasonably expects to pay at hire (SB 642, effective 2026). Give the range to applicants on request. Penalties are $100-$10,000 per violation.

Do not ask about prior pay, directly or through agents or background vendors. Asking about pay expectations is allowed. Voluntarily disclosed salary history cannot justify a pay gap under the Equal Pay Act.

No criminal history questions or checks before a conditional offer. Afterwards: a written individualized assessment, a preliminary notice with the report and 5 business days to respond (plus 5 more if disputing), then a final notice that mentions the right to file with CRD. Never ask about arrests without conviction or sealed or diverted records.

Give separate ICRAA and FCRA disclosures and obtain authorization. Credit checks are allowed only for listed roles, such as access to confidential or proprietary information or trade secrets, or $10,000+ in cash.
hiring.cite: Civ. Code 1786 et seq.; Labor Code 1024.5; FCRA

hiring.detail: CRD rules (effective 1 Oct 2025) make employers liable for discriminatory ADS, including when used by vendors acting as agents. Document anti-bias testing, offer accommodations, and keep ADS inputs and outputs for 4 years. CCPA ADMT pre-use notice and opt-out or appeal rights start 1 Jan 2027.

Do not reject candidates for off-duty cannabis use or non-psychoactive metabolite results, and do not ask about past use. Exceptions: roles requiring federal background investigations or security clearances, or testing required by federal contracts.
A posting may require a driver's license only if driving is reasonably expected in the job and other transport (e.g., rideshare or transit) would not be comparable in time and cost (from 2025).

Use E-Verify only as federal law requires, never before an offer or to check current employees. Give employees notice within 72 hours of a federal I-9 inspection notice. Do not voluntarily let immigration agents into non-public areas without a judicial warrant.
Give a CCPA notice at collection at or before collecting applicant data, including via ATS vendors, stating categories, purposes and retention periods. Keep applications 4 years.

Use CA-specific templates: no non-compete, no non-CA law or forum clause unless the employee has individual counsel, no training or relocation repayment clauses, and an at-will statement. The exempt salary must meet $70,304 (2026) or $72,384 (2027).

onboarding.detail: Give non-exempt hires written notice of pay rate(s), payday, employer legal names and addresses, workers' comp carrier, paid sick leave terms, and any applicable disaster declaration. Notify changes within 7 days.

CRD sexual harassment pamphlet (or equivalent), SDI (DE 2515) and PFL (DE 2511) brochures, workers' comp new-employee pamphlet, CRD victims' leave notice, and the lactation policy. Report new hires to EDD (DE 34) within 20 days.
onboarding.cite: Gov Code 12950; UI Code 2613; Labor Code 3551; Gov Code 12945.8

onboarding.req: SB 294 notice and emergency contact at hire
onboarding.detail: Give the Workplace Know Your Rights notice at hire. Collect an emergency contact and ask whether it may be notified if the employee is arrested or detained at work.
Assign 1-hour (non-supervisor) or 2-hour (supervisor) interactive training within 6 months of hire or promotion, and track the 2-year cycle per person. Keep certificates 2 years.

Proprietary information and invention agreements must attach or quote LC 2870: inventions made entirely on the employee's own time without company equipment or trade secrets are excluded unless they relate to company business or R&D or result from company work. Include a prior-inventions schedule.

NDAs and non-disparagement clauses must not stop employees from disclosing information about unlawful acts such as harassment or discrimination, and must include the statutory carve-out. Add a DTSA immunity notice to keep federal trade secret remedies.
Give employees and contractors a privacy notice covering HR, benefits, monitoring, badge and CCTV, and security data, with retention periods and how to exercise rights.

IIPP orientation, WVPP training (initial and then annual), HazCom and lab chemical hygiene training, and heat illness training where applicable. Record trainer, date, duration and competencies (SB 513).

Confirm each exempt hire meets both the salary floor and the duties test. Computer professionals need $58.85/hr or $122,573.13/yr (2026). Technicians and fab or lab operators are generally non-exempt.

payAndPayroll.detail: Non-exempt staff: at least twice monthly on designated paydays, within 7 days after the pay period closes. Exempt staff may be paid monthly. Post a notice of paydays and the time and place of payment.

Show gross and net wages, hours and all rates (non-exempt), deductions, pay period dates, employee name and last-4 SSN or ID, legal employer name and address, and the PSL balance. Penalties are $50 then $100 per pay period, up to $4,000 per employee, plus PAGA.

Pay 1.5x for hours over 8 in a day or 40 in a week and for the first 8 hours on the 7th consecutive day; pay 2x over 12 in a day and over 8 on the 7th day. Include non-discretionary bonuses and shift differentials in the regular rate. Alternative workweek schedules require a secret-ballot election and a DLSE filing.

Executive, administrative and professional exemptions require a salary of at least $70,304/yr (2026) and $72,384/yr (2027). The computer-professional exemption requires $58.85/hr or $122,573.13/yr (2026); DIR publishes the next rate each fall.

Pay one extra hour at the regular rate of compensation for each workday with a missed or late meal or rest break. Premiums are wages, so they must appear on wage statements and are included in final-pay calculations.

Reimburse all necessary business expenses, including a reasonable percentage of personal phone and internet for remote or hybrid staff and mileage. A stipend is acceptable if it fully covers actual expenses.

Pay for substantially similar work may not differ by sex, race or ethnicity unless explained by bona fide factors. From 2026, 'wages' includes bonuses, stock and options, and benefits; the limitation period is 3 years with recovery back up to 6 years. Run privileged pay equity audits.

100+ employees must file with CRD by the second Wednesday of May (13 May 2026; 12 May 2027). Penalties are mandatory under SB 464. The 2027 report moves to 23 SOC-based job categories with mandatory exempt status, employment type and weeks worked.

payAndPayroll.req: Local minimum wage for non-exempt staff
payAndPayroll.detail: Apply the highest applicable rate by work location: Sunnyvale $19.50, Mountain View $19.70, Santa Clara $18.70, San Jose $18.45 (2026). Watch 1 July changes in SF, LA and Berkeley. Relevant for interns, technicians and admin staff.

No deductions for cash shortages, breakage or equipment loss unless caused by dishonesty, willful act or gross negligence. No deductions from final pay for unreturned equipment without lawful authorization.

timeAndLeave.detail: At least 40 hours/5 days usable per year, with an accrual cap of at least 80 hours/10 days or front-loading. Uses include care for self or family (including a designated person), victim needs, jury and witness duty (AB 406, from 1 Oct 2025) and victims' court proceedings (from 1 Jan 2026). Pay by the next payday. The January 2026 DLSE poster is required.

5+ employees; the employee needs 12 months' service and 1,250 hours. 12 weeks of job-protected leave for own or family serious health condition (including grandparent, sibling, adult child, designated person), bonding, or military exigency. Health coverage continues during leave.
Up to 4 months per pregnancy (5+ employees, no service requirement), separate from and in addition to CFRA bonding. Health coverage continues. Includes reasonable accommodation and transfer.

EDD pays PFL for up to 8 weeks and SDI for up to 52 weeks, replacing 70-90% of wages since 2025 (maximum weekly benefit $1,765 in 2026). Employers cannot require vacation to be used first (AB 2123, 2025). PFL for a designated person starts 1 Jul 2028 (SB 590).
timeAndLeave.cite: UI Code 2601 et seq., 3301 (SB 951, AB 2123, SB 590)

timeAndLeave.detail: 5 days of bereavement within 3 months of a family member's death (documentation may be requested). 5 days per reproductive-loss event (miscarriage, stillbirth, failed adoption or surrogacy, failed ART), max 20 days in 12 months, kept confidential. Both apply to 5+ employers after 30 days' service.

Job-protected leave and safety accommodations for victims of qualifying acts of violence and their family members, plus jury and witness leave. Employees may use PSL or vacation. Enforced by CRD since 2025.

25+ employees at a location: up to 40 hours/year (8 hours/month) for school or child-care activities and emergencies. Kin care lets employees use half their annual sick leave accrual for family members.

Voting (up to 2 hours paid). Military spouse leave, 10 days unpaid (25+ employees). Organ donor leave, 30 business days paid plus 30 unpaid, and bone marrow donor leave, 5 days paid (15+ employees). Civil Air Patrol, volunteer firefighter, rehab (25+) and literacy leave.
timeAndLeave.cite: Elections Code 14000; Mil. & Vet. Code 395.10; Labor Code 1508-1513, 1025, 1041, 230.3, 1501

timeAndLeave.detail: Reasonable break time each time the employee needs to express milk, in a private non-bathroom space near the work area with a surface, seating, electricity, and access to a sink and refrigerator. Unpaid if it exceeds the paid rest break.
No forfeiture of accrued vacation. Caps are allowed. Pay out accrued unused vacation at separation at the final rate. For unlimited PTO, document that it is not earned and not capped.
timeAndLeave.cite: Labor Code 227.3; McPherson v. EF Intercultural (2020)

benefits.detail: Withhold 1.3% of all wages in 2026 (no taxable wage ceiling since 2024; covers DI and PFL). A voluntary plan is possible with EDD approval.
Employer-paid on the first $7,000 per employee per year; the UI rate is experience-rated (3.4% for new employers) and ETT is 0.1%. File DE 9/DE 9C quarterly.
Insurance or self-insurance is mandatory. Give the DWC-1 claim form within 1 working day of learning of an injury. Post the carrier notice.

Employers with 1+ employee that do not offer a qualified plan must register and facilitate CalSavers payroll deductions. Employers offering a 401(k) should file the exemption to avoid penalty notices.

Federal COBRA applies at 20+ employees and Cal-COBRA covers insured plans with 2-19. At termination, give the HIPP notice and the LC 2800.2 conversion/continuation notice. Keep group health coverage in place during CFRA and PDL.
benefits.cite: Labor Code 2800.2; Welf. & Inst. Code 14124.94; Health & Safety Code 1366.20 et seq.

benefits.detail: California's individual mandate requires minimum essential coverage information (e.g., Forms 1094/1095) to be filed with the Franchise Tax Board by 31 March for self-insured plans; insurers file for insured plans.
Employers with 50+ full-time employees in the Bay Area Air District must offer a qualifying commuter benefit (pre-tax, subsidy, or shuttle). San Francisco has a separate 20+ employee ordinance.
benefits.cite: Gov Code 65081; BAAQMD Reg. 14 Rule 1; SF Env. Code ch. 4

benefits.detail: Employers with 20+ employees must make health care expenditures for SF-based employees (HCSO) at the rates set each year.

Stock and options are 'wages' for Equal Pay Act purposes from 2026. Forfeiture of unvested equity is generally allowed, but clawback or repayment of paid or vested amounts at departure may be caught by AB 692 and needs counsel review.

performanceAndConduct.detail: Investigate complaints promptly and impartially with trained investigators, document findings, and take proportionate remedial action. Claimants have 3 years to file with CRD.

Adverse action within 90 days of wage, whistleblower or equal-pay protected activity creates a rebuttable presumption of retaliation, with up to $10,000 penalty per LC 1102.5 violation. Have legal review terminations that fall in this window.

performanceAndConduct.req: Human review of AI in discipline
performanceAndConduct.detail: Under CRD rules, discriminatory ADS outcomes are FEHA violations; keep a human decision-maker and documented rationale. SB 947 (pending, effective 1 Jul 2027 if signed) would bar relying mainly on ADS for discipline or termination without human review and require post-use notice.
No adverse action for lawful off-duty, off-premises conduct, political activity or affiliation, or off-duty cannabis use. Employees may discuss their wages.
Do not ask for personal social media passwords or access. Investigations of personal accounts must be narrowly limited to alleged misconduct.
Hold a timely, good-faith interactive process for disability, pregnancy or religious needs, including alternatives to AI assessments. Failing to engage is a separate violation.
SB 399 (LC 1137) is preliminarily enjoined (Oct 2025; Ninth Circuit argued July 2026). The prudent course is to keep attendance at meetings on union or political topics voluntary.
performanceAndConduct.cite: Labor Code 1137; CalChamber v. Bonta (E.D. Cal.)

performanceAndConduct.detail: Random testing is limited by the constitutional privacy right to safety-sensitive roles. Reasonable-suspicion testing needs documented impairment signs. Offer rehab accommodation (LC 1025, 25+ employees).
performanceAndConduct.cite: Cal. Const. art. I §1; Labor Code 1025

termination.detail: Document legitimate business reasons and check timing against leave, accommodation requests, complaints and pay inquiries. Wrongful termination in violation of public policy (Tameny) and FEHA claims are common and can carry punitive damages.

termination.req: Final pay on the last day
termination.detail: On discharge or layoff, pay all wages, accrued vacation or PTO, premiums and commissions due immediately. Arrange final checks or authorized direct deposit before termination meetings, including remote ones.

Covered establishments (75+ employees in the prior 12 months, counting those with 6+ months' service) must give 60 days' notice for 50+ layoffs within 30 days (any percentage), relocations of 100+ miles, or closures. Notice goes to employees, EDD, the Local Workforce Development Board and local chief elected officials. SB 617 content applies from 2026.
Federal WARN (100+ employees). OWBPA for workers aged 40+: 21 days to consider individual releases (45 days for groups, with decisional-unit disclosures) and 7 days to revoke.
Run privileged adverse-impact analysis on RIF selections by FEHA category, including age 40+, and check for disproportionate impact on employees on leave.

Do not try to enforce non-competes, customer or employee non-solicits, or similar restraints against California workers, even under an out-of-state agreement. Doing so risks the worker's attorney fees and unfair-competition liability.

For agreements from 1 Jan 2026, do not demand repayment of training, relocation or other costs, or 'quit fees', at separation unless an AB 692 exception applies. AB 1697 (on the Governor's desk) would move the start date to 1 Jan 2027.
Give the UI Code 1089 written notice of the change in employment status and the EDD DE 2320 pamphlet immediately, plus the HIPP notice and COBRA or Cal-COBRA notice.
termination.cite: UI Code 1089; 22 CCR 1089-1; Welf. & Inst. Code 14124.94

exit.detail: Include all wages, accrued vacation, overtime, meal and rest premiums, earned commissions, and a final itemized wage statement. Reimburse outstanding expenses promptly.

With 72+ hours' notice, pay on the last day. Without notice, pay within 72 hours (mail if the employee requests). If the employer moves up the separation date, treat it as a discharge and pay immediately.
COBRA or Cal-COBRA election notices, HIPP notice, conversion notice, and equity plan exercise-window information (e.g., the ISO 90-day rule).

exit.req: Return of property and trade-secret exit
exit.detail: Get signed certification that devices and documents have been returned, remind the employee of confidentiality and CUTSA duties, and revoke access immediately. Forensically image devices where risk is high. Do not withhold final pay for unreturned items.
exit.cite: Civ. Code 3426 et seq.; Labor Code 221

exit.detail: Personnel file within 30 days (one request per year for former employees), payroll records within 21 days, and signed documents on request. From 2026, training records must include trainer, date, duration, competencies and certifications.
Truthful, good-faith references are privileged, but misrepresentations meant to stop someone getting a job are prohibited. Many employers confirm dates and title only.
Settlement agreements with employees who filed good-faith claims cannot bar rehire, except in limited cases such as a documented finding of sexual harassment or assault.
Handle post-exit CCPA access and deletion requests, apply legal holds, and follow the retention schedule. Keep ADS and personnel data 4 years.

recordsAndPrivacy.detail: Give notice at collection and a privacy policy. Honor requests to know, delete, correct and limit use of sensitive personal information within 45 days, subject to employment-law exceptions. Put CCPA terms in service-provider contracts and do not sell or share HR data.

recordsAndPrivacy.req: CPPA risk assessments and cybersecurity audits
recordsAndPrivacy.detail: From 1 Jan 2026, run risk assessments before high-risk processing, such as ADMT for employment decisions, systematic observation used to infer employee traits (e.g., productivity monitoring), or processing sensitive data beyond payroll or legal needs. Existing processing must be assessed by 31 Dec 2027; attestations are due 1 Apr 2028. The first cybersecurity audit is due 1 Apr 2028 if revenue exceeds $100M.

ADMT used for 'significant decisions' (hiring, work allocation, compensation, promotion, discipline, termination) needs a pre-use notice, opt-out (or a qualifying human appeal or exception), and access and explanation rights. Inventory HR AI tools in 2026.

Allow inspection or copies within 30 calendar days of a written request (extendable to 35 by agreement). The file now includes education and training records (SB 513). Keep 3 years after termination. The penalty is $750.
Provide wage statement and payroll records within 21 calendar days of request. Keep at least 3 years (4 recommended because of the UCL limitation period). The penalty is $750.

Keep applications, personnel, referral and ADS data 4 years; job title and wage history for employment plus 3 years; PSL records 3 years; harassment training 2 years; WVPP records 5 years (training 1 year); SB 294 notices 3 years.
Store race, ethnicity and sex data collected for pay data reporting separately from personnel files (SB 464, from 2026).
Keep medical information in separate confidential files and do not use or disclose it without authorization. Keep reproductive-loss and victim-status information confidential.

No audio or video in restrooms, locker rooms or changing rooms. Recording confidential communications needs all-party consent. Electronic vehicle tracking is limited to owned or leased vehicles. Disclose monitoring in the CCPA notice.

healthSafety.detail: Written program with a responsible person, periodic inspections, hazard correction, training when hired or reassigned and when new hazards arise, and a way for employees to report hazards without reprisal.

Site-specific WVPP (in the IIPP or standalone) developed with employee input, with annual interactive training, a violent incident log, post-incident investigation, annual plan review, and employee access to records within 15 days. Cal/OSHA's general-industry standard must be adopted by 31 Dec 2026; the April 2026 draft expands obligations.
Employers may seek workplace violence restraining orders for employees, and since 2025 may also seek them for harassment. Collective bargaining representatives may also file.

At 82°F provide water, cool-down areas, acclimatization, training and emergency procedures. At 87°F, or 82°F with heat-restrictive clothing such as clean-room garments or radiant heat, assess and apply engineering and administrative controls.
Hazard Communication program and SDS access; chemical hygiene plan for laboratories; Prop 65 warnings; specific standards for toxic gases and hazardous materials in fabs and labs.

Keep Forms 300/301 for 5 years and post the 300A from 1 Feb to 30 Apr. Submit electronically through OSHA ITA by 2 March where covered. Report serious injuries, illnesses or deaths to Cal/OSHA within 8 hours.

Employees may refuse to report to, or may leave, a workplace during an emergency condition such as a disaster or violent act if they reasonably believe it is unsafe. Employers cannot bar mobile phone use to seek help.
Address repetitive motion injuries in production, lab and office work. Include home-office ergonomics guidance and pay for necessary equipment under LC 2802.

healthSafety.req: Emergency action and fire prevention plans
healthSafety.detail: Written emergency action and fire prevention plans, evacuation drills, and first aid supplies and trained responders appropriate to site hazards.

terminationDeepDive.voluntary: Employees may resign at any time with no notice (at-will), and employers may not require notice or impose financial penalties for leaving (AB 692 bans 'quit fees'). If the employee gives 72+ hours' notice, final pay is due on the last day; without notice, within 72 hours. If the employer accepts the resignation early, pay through the notice period or treat it as a discharge and pay immediately. Paid garden leave during a notice period is allowed, but no post-employment non-compete or non-solicit can follow it.
terminationDeepDive.involuntary: At-will termination needs no cause or process, but litigation risk is high. Main exposures are FEHA discrimination, retaliation and failure-to-accommodate claims (5+ employees); wrongful termination in violation of public policy; whistleblower retaliation, with a presumption within 90 days of protected activity; CFRA/PDL interference; and PAGA wage claims raised after termination. Best practice: documented performance history, consistent treatment, legal review of timing, a decision-maker independent of any complainant, human review of any AI/ADS input, and final pay ready at the meeting.
terminationDeepDive.redundancy: There is no statutory redundancy pay or consultation. Cal-WARN (LC 1400-1408): covered establishments (75+ employees in the prior 12 months) must give 60 days' written notice before a mass layoff (50+ employees within 30 days, regardless of percentage), relocation (100+ miles) or termination. Notice goes to affected employees, EDD, the Local Workforce Development Board, and the chief elected officials of the city and county. From 2026 (SB 617), notices must say whether the employer will coordinate rapid-response services within 30 days and include board contact details and CalFresh information. Federal WARN and OWBPA group disclosures also apply. Remedies are back pay and benefits for up to 60 days plus a $500/day civil penalty. SB 951 (pending) would add AI-related layoff disclosures.
terminationDeepDive.finalPayTiming: Discharge or layoff: all earned wages, including accrued vacation/PTO and meal/rest premiums, are due immediately at the time of termination (LC 201, 227.3). Resignation: due on the last day if 72+ hours' notice was given, otherwise within 72 hours; mail if the employee asks (LC 202). Late payment triggers waiting-time penalties of one day's wages for each day late, up to 30 days (LC 203). It can also bring wage statement penalties (LC 226) and PAGA penalties. Direct deposit of final pay is allowed only with prior employee authorization and funds available on time.
requiredDocuments: Final paycheck with itemized wage statement (LC 201-203, 226)
Written notice of change in employment relationship (UI Code 1089)
HIPP (Health Insurance Premium Payment) notice (Welf. & Inst. Code 14124.94)
COBRA or Cal-COBRA continuation notice and LC 2800.2 conversion notice
Cal-WARN notice with SB 617 content, where applicable
OWBPA disclosures for releases from workers aged 40+ (21/45 days plus 7-day revocation)
Personnel file, payroll records and signed documents on request (LC 1198.5, 226(b), 432)
terminationDeepDive.releaseAgreements: Releases are enforceable if knowing and voluntary and supported by consideration beyond wages already owed. Include an express Civil Code 1542 waiver of unknown claims. Undisputed wages cannot be released (LC 206.5), so pay all final wages unconditionally. Some rights cannot be waived: LC 2802 reimbursement, workers' comp (needs WCAB approval), unemployment, and representative PAGA claims. Non-disparagement or confidentiality terms need the Gov Code 12964.5 carve-out ('Nothing in this agreement prevents you from discussing or disclosing information about unlawful acts in the workplace…'). The employee must be told they may consult an attorney and given at least 5 business days to consider. Code Civ. Proc. 1001 bars confidentiality of facts in filed sexual harassment or discrimination claims (the amount can stay confidential), and 1002.5 bars no-rehire clauses. For age 40+, OWBPA requires 21/45 days to consider and 7 days to revoke.
terminationDeepDive.typicalPackage: Market practice (not statutory) for California tech and semiconductor employers: individual contributors typically get 2-4 weeks' base pay per year of service with a 4-8 week minimum; directors and VPs 3-6 months; executives 6-12+ months under a severance plan. Packages often add 3-6 months of COBRA subsidy, outplacement, and sometimes a pro-rated bonus. Equity acceleration is generally limited to change-of-control double-trigger plans. RIFs subject to Cal-WARN often pay 60 days of pay in lieu of working notice plus severance in exchange for a release.

recentChanges.title: 2027 minimum wage set at $17.40; exempt floor rises to $72,384
recentChanges.detail: DIR announced the statewide minimum wage will rise from $16.90 (2026) to $17.40 on 1 Jan 2027, lifting the exempt salary floor from $70,304 to $72,384. The 2026 computer-professional rate is $58.85/hr ($122,573.13/yr); DIR publishes the 2027 rate in the fall.

recentChanges.title: SB 294 Workplace Know Your Rights Act in force
recentChanges.detail: Annual stand-alone notice (Labor Commissioner template) due to all employees by 1 Feb 2026 and each year after, and at hire. Emergency contact designation offered by 30 Mar 2026, with notification if an employee is arrested or detained at work. Penalties up to $500 per employee; emergency contact violations up to $10,000 per employee.

recentChanges.title: SB 642: pay scale 'good faith estimate'; broader Equal Pay Act
recentChanges.detail: Pay scale now means a good-faith estimate of the salary or hourly range the employer reasonably expects to pay at hire. The Equal Pay Act now covers pay differences by 'another sex', defines wages to include bonuses, stock and options, and benefits, extends the limitation period to 3 years, and allows recovery back up to 6 years.

recentChanges.title: AB 692 bans stay-or-pay and repayment clauses
recentChanges.detail: For agreements entered on or after 1 Jan 2026 (B&P 16608, LC 926), employers cannot require repayment of training, relocation or other debts, or quit or replacement fees, when employment ends. Narrow exceptions cover transferable-credential tuition and discretionary upfront bonuses under standalone agreements. Minimum damages are $5,000 per worker, plus attorney fees.

recentChanges.title: CPPA regulations: risk assessments now, ADMT 2027, cyber audits 2028
recentChanges.detail: Approved by OAL on 22 Sep 2025 and effective 1 Jan 2026. Risk assessments are required for high-risk processing, including employee monitoring and ADMT for employment decisions. ADMT notice, opt-out or appeal, and access duties start 1 Jan 2027. Risk-assessment attestations and the first cybersecurity audits (revenue over $100M) are due 1 Apr 2028.

recentChanges.title: SB 464 pay data changes
recentChanges.detail: Penalties for failing to file pay data reports are now mandatory, and demographic data must be stored separately from personnel files. From the 2027 report, 23 SOC-based job categories replace the 10 EEO-1 categories, and exempt status, employment type and weeks worked become mandatory fields.

recentChanges.title: SB 513 training records added to personnel files
recentChanges.detail: Training records must now record employee name, trainer or provider, date and duration, core competencies (including equipment or software skills), and any certification. They are available through LC 1198.5 requests, answered within 30 days.

recentChanges.title: SB 617 expands Cal-WARN notice content
recentChanges.detail: Cal-WARN notices must now say whether the employer will coordinate rapid-response services (within 30 days), include Local Workforce Development Board contacts, and describe CalFresh.

recentChanges.title: Captive-audience ban and PERB backstop enjoined
recentChanges.detail: A federal court enjoined SB 399 (LC 1137) in Oct 2025; the Ninth Circuit heard argument in July 2026. In late Dec 2025 a federal court largely enjoined AB 288, which would have let PERB hear private-sector labor disputes, as NLRA-preempted.

recentChanges.title: CRD automated-decision systems regulations effective
recentChanges.detail: FEHA rules effective 1 Oct 2025 cover AI and algorithmic tools in hiring, promotion and pay. Employers are liable for agents such as vendors, anti-bias testing is relevant to defenses, and ADS data must be kept 4 years. The Governor vetoed SB 7 ('No Robo Bosses Act') in Oct 2025.

recentChanges.title: AB 406 expands paid sick leave uses
recentChanges.detail: PSL may be used for jury service and witness appearances from 1 Oct 2025 (urgency statute), and for attending judicial proceedings about crimes against the employee or family members from 1 Jan 2026. The DLSE issued a new PSL poster in Jan 2026.

recentChanges.title: Victims' leave moved to FEHA; PFL and driver's license changes
recentChanges.detail: AB 2499 moved and expanded victims' leave and safety accommodations into Gov Code 12945.8, enforced by CRD, with a new notice duty. AB 2123 bars requiring vacation before PFL. SB 1100 limits driver's license requirements in job postings.

recentChanges.title: Workplace Violence Prevention Plans and indoor heat standard
recentChanges.detail: Since 1 Jul 2024 (SB 553, LC 6401.9) most employers need a WVPP, training, an incident log and 5-year records. The indoor heat standard (8 CCR 3396) took effect 23 Jul 2024.

recentChanges.title: PAGA reform
recentChanges.detail: For notices filed from 19 Jun 2024: penalties are capped at 15% or 30% for employers that took 'all reasonable steps' to comply, cure procedures apply, standing is limited to violations the plaintiff personally suffered, early evaluation conferences are available, and the employee share is 35%.

recentChanges.title: 2024 package: PSL 40 hours, non-compete notices, cannabis, reproductive loss
recentChanges.detail: SB 616 raised PSL to 40 hours/5 days. SB 699 and AB 1076 required non-compete void notices by 14 Feb 2024. AB 2188 and SB 700 protect off-duty cannabis use. SB 848 created reproductive loss leave. SB 497 created a 90-day retaliation presumption.

watchlist.title: AB 1697: AB 692 stay-or-pay reset
watchlist.detail: An urgency bill, presented to the Governor 3 Sep 2026. It would move AB 692's start to 1 Jan 2027, remove 2026 exposure, extend the bonus exception to retention bonuses, and add exceptions for grant-funded bonuses, advanced PTO (up to 40 hours) and financial-services inducements.
watchlist.expected: Governor action by 30 Sep 2026; effective immediately if signed

watchlist.title: SB 947: No Robo Bosses Act of 2026
watchlist.detail: Would bar relying mainly on ADS for discipline or termination without human review and corroboration, bar predictive or retaliatory ADS uses, and require post-use written notice and data access. Civil penalty $500 per violation.
watchlist.expected: Governor action by 30 Sep 2026; operative 1 Jul 2027 if signed

watchlist.title: Other bills awaiting the Governor
watchlist.detail: SB 951 (WARN disclosure for AI-driven layoffs), SB 1149 (bereavement for a designated person), AB 1940 (menopause as sex discrimination), AB 1331 and AB 1883 (bathroom surveillance; neural or emotion-recognition surveillance), SB 1237 (higher pay data penalties), and AB 1803 (anti-hate content in harassment training, 2028).
watchlist.expected: Governor action by 30 Sep 2026; most effective 1 Jan 2027

watchlist.title: Cal/OSHA general-industry workplace violence standard
watchlist.detail: The Standards Board must adopt a WVP regulation by 31 Dec 2026. The April 2026 draft narrows the small-employer exemption, covers employer-provided transportation, and expands hazard assessment and recordkeeping.
watchlist.expected: Adoption by 31 Dec 2026; effective date TBD

watchlist.title: SB 399 captive-audience appeal
watchlist.detail: The Ninth Circuit heard argument in July 2026 on the preliminary injunction against LC 1137, and the panel appeared skeptical of the law.

watchlist.title: CCPA ADMT compliance and first risk-assessment filings
watchlist.detail: Inventory HR AI and ADMT tools and build notice, opt-out or appeal workflows by 1 Jan 2027. Complete risk assessments for existing processing by 31 Dec 2027 and file attestations by 1 Apr 2028.

watchlist.title: 2027 pay data report format
watchlist.detail: The first report under SB 464's 23 SOC-based job categories, with mandatory exempt status, employment type and weeks-worked fields. Map HRIS job codes in 2026.

watchlist.title: PFL for designated persons
watchlist.detail: SB 590 extends PFL wage replacement to care for a 'designated person' (blood relative or family-equivalent). Align CFRA and PSL designated-person procedures.

calendar.title: New laws, minimum wage and exempt thresholds effective
calendar.detail: 1 Jan: state minimum wage ($17.40 in 2027), exempt salary floor ($72,384 in 2027), computer-professional rate update, and many local minimum wages. Update posters, pay scales in postings, and CA offer and agreement templates.

calendar.title: SB 294 notice; Cal/OSHA 300A posting
calendar.detail: By 1 Feb: annual Workplace Know Your Rights notice to all employees and to any union. Post Form 300A from 1 Feb to 30 Apr.

calendar.title: OSHA ITA upload; FTB health coverage reporting
calendar.detail: 2 Mar: electronic injury data submission where covered. 31 Mar: Forms 1094/1095 to the Franchise Tax Board (self-insured plans).

calendar.title: Pay data preparation
calendar.detail: Freeze the snapshot-period data, map job categories (23 SOC categories from 2027), check the separately stored demographic data, and prepare the labor-contractor report.

calendar.title: CRD pay data report due
calendar.detail: Due the second Wednesday of May (13 May 2026; 12 May 2027) for employers with 100+ employees and those using 100+ labor-contractor workers.

calendar.title: Mid-year leave and PSL audit
calendar.detail: Check PSL balances on wage statements, CFRA/PDL tracking, and local ordinance rates ahead of July changes.

calendar.title: Local minimum wage changes; WVPP annual review
calendar.detail: 1 Jul: local minimum wage and ordinance changes (e.g., SF, LA, Berkeley). Many employers review their WVPP around its 1 Jul 2024 anniversary; review at least annually and after incidents.

calendar.title: Next-year minimum wage announced
calendar.detail: By 1 Aug the Department of Finance and DIR announce the next year's minimum wage. Budget exempt salary increases to stay above 2x minimum wage.

calendar.title: Governor bill-signing deadline
calendar.detail: 30 Sep (even years; mid-Oct in odd years): final signatures and vetoes. Start the new-law implementation plan for 1 Jan.

calendar.title: Computer professional rate; open enrollment
calendar.detail: DIR announces the next year's computer-professional exemption rate (usually Oct/Nov). Benefits open enrollment. Check CalSavers exemption status.

calendar.title: Local rate announcements; harassment training cohorts
calendar.detail: Bay Area cities announce 1 Jan minimum wages. Schedule harassment prevention training for employees whose 2-year cycle ends next year.

calendar.title: Year-end compliance
calendar.detail: Deliver annual WVPP refresher training, update the CCPA employee notice and retention schedule, finish CPPA risk assessments (existing processing due 31 Dec 2027), and reset PSL for front-load plans.

gotchas: Using national offer letter or PIIA templates in California: non-competes, Delaware or Texas choice-of-law or forum clauses, training or relocation repayment terms and liquidated damages are void or create penalties (B&P 16600.5, LC 925, AB 692).

Treating engineers, interns and technicians as exempt without checking both the salary floor ($70,304 in 2026; computer professional $58.85/hr) and the California duties tests, which are stricter than the federal ones.
Missing immediate final pay at layoffs and remote terminations, or leaving out accrued vacation or meal/rest premiums. This leads to 30 days of waiting-time penalties per employee and PAGA claims.
Using 'use-it-or-lose-it' vacation or loosely defined unlimited PTO, which triggers vacation payout liability at exit.
Posting CA-eligible or remote jobs without a good-faith pay range, or with a range far wider than what will actually be paid (SB 642).
Assuming CCPA does not cover HR data: no employee or applicant notice at collection, no process for DSARs on HR data, no retention schedule, and no assessment of AI hiring or monitoring tools.
Separation agreements without the Gov Code 12964.5 carve-out and 5-business-day attorney-consultation notice, without a Civil Code 1542 waiver, or with no-rehire clauses.
Not reimbursing remote or hybrid workers for phone, internet and home-office costs (LC 2802), and not paying meal/rest premiums to non-exempt lab and fab staff.
Ignoring local ordinances (Sunnyvale, Mountain View, San Jose and SF minimum wages; SF HCSO and Fair Chance; Bay Area commuter benefit) and assuming the state rules are the maximum.
Running pre-offer criminal checks or asking about cannabis use in global ATS workflows, which breaks the Fair Chance Act and Gov Code 12954.
semiconductorNotes: Trade secret strategy without non-competes: because B&P 16600 voids non-competes and most non-solicits, and California rejects 'inevitable disclosure', protect IP through CUTSA/DTSA-ready controls. Use tiered access, DLP, logging, exit certifications, device imaging for high-risk departures, and prompt TRO action. When hiring from competitors, use clean-room onboarding with no-bring certifications.

Invention assignment: PIIAs must include the LC 2870 carve-out notice (LC 2872). The carve-out does not protect inventions that relate to the employer's chip design business or R&D, so define the business scope clearly and collect prior-invention schedules. Moonlighting on unrelated projects cannot be banned outright, but use of company EDA tools, IP or time can be restricted.

Engineer classification: most design and verification engineers are exempt as learned professionals (or administrative) if paid at least $70,304 (2026) and they exercise discretion. The computer-professional exemption (LC 515.5, $58.85/hr) suits software, firmware and EDA roles but not hardware design as such. Lab technicians, test and fab operators and new-grad support roles are usually non-exempt: daily OT, meal/rest premiums, alternative workweek elections for 12-hour fab shifts.

Retention design after AB 692: replace clawback-style sign-on and retention bonuses and tuition repayment with forward-looking vesting (RSUs, deferred cash earned over time), or use standalone agreements that fit the statutory exceptions. Track AB 1697 (to the Governor by 30 Sep 2026), which would extend the exception to retention bonuses.

Lab and clean-room safety: the IIPP must cover HazCom (8 CCR 5194), the laboratory chemical hygiene plan (5191), toxic and pyrophoric gases, lasers and radiation, and Prop 65. Clean-room gowning can count as 'clothing that restricts heat removal' under the indoor heat standard, so it applies at 82°F.

Campus workplace violence plans: each campus or building needs a site-specific WVPP with badge and access control, visitor and contractor procedures, an insider-threat link to security, and a violent incident log. Annual interactive training and incident investigations must feed hazard correction. Coordinate with the SB 294 emergency-contact process for law-enforcement detentions on site.

Export control versus FEHA: EAR/ITAR deemed-export licensing can justify asking about citizenship or immigration status only as far as needed for licensing. Do this after the offer where possible, and avoid blanket national-origin or citizenship screens, which are FEHA and IRCA risks. The cannabis-protection exception covers roles needing federal security clearances or background investigations.

AI in engineering talent processes: resume screeners, coding-assessment scoring and attrition-prediction tools are ADS under CRD rules (bias testing, 4-year records) and ADMT under CCPA from 2027. Productivity or telemetry monitoring of engineers may require a CPPA risk assessment.
